# Sasu

> Free, open-source voice assistant for Mac (Apple Silicon, macOS 13+). Say "Hey Sasu" in English, Tamil (தமிழ்) or Tanglish to open apps, control music and volume, sort files, set reminders and more. Developed by Sarangan Raviraj. MIT license.

Key facts:
- Voice recognition, the wake word and voiceprints run on the Mac; only the text of a request goes to the AI the user picks (free Google Gemini or Groq, Anthropic Claude, or Ollama offline).
- Only the owner's voice gets full access; family and kid profiles get limited access; strangers get guest mode.
- Amma mode for elderly parents: slow Tamil speech and large captions, medicine reminders that ask "did you take it?" and text the family on a missed dose, calling family by voice, and a spoken "help" alert.
- Tamil Panchangam: Rahu kaalam, Yamagandam, Kuligai, thithi and the Tamil date for the home city, computed on the Mac.
- A scam checker ("Sasu, idhu scam-aa?") that flags OTP requests, fake bank links, prize and "digital arrest" messages, offline first.
- Agent features: screen control (clicks and fills an app's own buttons and fields by number, asking before each step, never password fields), desktop tidy, watch & tell (downloads, battery, price drops, commands), and scheduled tasks that never auto-approve risky steps.
- Risky actions need Touch ID; every action can be undone ("Sasu, undo"); a hash-chained log records everything.
